note: Structured state for known gaps/exclusions/risks — CONSUMED by tests/expected_fails_check.d (schema + kind + probe-target existence). Each entry has an id, area, reason, since, remove_when, and a `kind`: `permanent_exclusion` (not public API / platform), `known_gap` (a generator limitation with no failing target), or `risk` (a private-API dependency that MUST keep compiling — its `probe_targets` name the build targets that guard it, and the checker verifies those targets exist).

entries.reason: QUiLoader-only private Qt widgets (QFileDialog internals, QtGradient editors, qprintpropertieswidget) are not public API, so the differential oracle can't hold them.
entries.remove_when: never (these are not public Qt API)

entries.reason: An overridden virtual that returns a container/QList still dispatches non-virtually — the C++ method shim can't sret those, so it falls back to the direct-symbol guard. No known Qt override is affected.
entries.remove_when: a container/QList-return-capable virtual shim lands

entries.reason: A method with a move-only (deleted-copy) by-value param uses the direct pragma decl, or is dropped if inline — the shim/guard would copy the param.
entries.remove_when: the shim forwards value params by std::move

entries.reason: Linux/POSIX is Tier 1; Windows/MSVC-x64 is a documented roadmap (docs/windows-roadmap.md), not tested.
entries.remove_when: the windows-roadmap tiers are implemented and green

entries.reason: qmlRegisterType fills QQmlPrivate::RegisterType and calls QQmlPrivate::qmlregister — a private struct whose layout differs Qt5<->Qt6 (handled behind a QT_VERSION seam) and can shift between Qt minor versions.
entries.remove_when: Qt exposes a public API to register a runtime QMetaObject as a QML type, or the probe runs across a Qt-version matrix in CI

entries.reason: All D @QObject types registered via qmlRegisterType share one C++ typeId (QtdMocObject* on Qt6, QObjectStar on Qt5), differing only by runtime QMetaObject. On Qt6 this makes a TYPED cross-property assignment (`property Alpha a: Alpha{}`) fail QML's metatype assignability check. Instantiation and `property var` work on both; the qmltwo test proves N distinct types coexist.
entries.remove_when: each registered runtime type gets a DISTINCT QMetaType (a dynamic QMetaTypeInterface per type) instead of the shared carrier metatype

entries.reason: .qmltypes validation uses QQmlJSTypeDescriptionReader from Qt6QmlCompiler private API (the reader qmllint/qmltyperegistrar use). Qt6-only; can change across versions.
entries.remove_when: a public qmltypes parser ships, or the probe runs across a Qt-version matrix

entries.reason: The runtime moc (qtdmoc.cpp) builds QMetaObjects with QMetaObjectBuilder, a Qt private API. Long-standing dependency; every moc/qml/tr target compiles against it.
entries.remove_when: never expected (no public equivalent); revisit if Qt ships a public runtime-metaobject builder

entries.reason: The `-all-` (--objpaths/--dumpall) target is not built for 2 fixtures, and it is not a gap: a `Connections` element is desugared into connects and no object is built, while the engine holds one in `conn` — both fixtures say so in their own headers. Connect, CrossCall. Permanent for this protocol. Everything else this entry once listed is DONE (2026-08-03): ALIASES (qtmoc gained @PropertyAlias — a forwarding property backed by a getter and a `<name>_set`, for a scalar target and for an object one); DEFAULT-PROPERTY HOLDERS (a declared object property exists even when its type maps to no D wrapper, and a single-object default property is ASSIGNED, not only appended); LIST PROPERTIES (a meta-object QQmlListProperty whose elements the runtime owns — it needs the metatype AND the element type registered with QQmlMetaType, and the registration has to run from a function because --gc-sections removes a file-scope static nothing reads); and the `__class` label, now decided in the emitter. Measured: controls 23 of 23, quick 46 of 46, corpus 44 of 46.
entries.remove_when: never for the Connections pair — it is a deliberate structural difference.

entries.reason: The WEAK protocol's independent half (`--verify-props`) fails when the engine built a QML-declared member no label mentions. An item a VIEW creates has no static path, so `--labels` drops it by design, and a delegate that declares properties trips a guard that was never able to name those objects at all -- it is not the "both sides shrank" case the guard exists to catch. `labelsGap` in reggaefile.d exempts exactly the five delegate fixtures (QDelegateKidCtx, QDelegateRole, QDelegateRoleReq, QDelegateReqNoModel, QDelegateReqFill) from that half only; the diff of the values it DID record still runs, and the STRONG `-all-` target beside it compares those items properly and is green for all five.
entries.remove_when: `--labels` can name an object a view creates (it would need the index the view decides, which is what `--objpaths`/`--dumpall` already asks at run time)

entries.reason: The node that generates a fixture's D treats exit 3 (PARTIAL: members skipped and reported) as failure, deliberately, so no fixture can quietly go partial. Two fixtures cannot satisfy that because their REFUSAL is what they measure: QDelegateReqNoModel (a delegate declaring required properties has no `model` to read, and reading the context there would invent a value the engine does not have) and QDelegateReqFill (same boundary, from the other side). `partialOk` in reggaefile.d accepts 0 or 3 for those two and nothing else; the differential beside them is what proves the refusal is the RIGHT one, both sides reading empty.
entries.remove_when: required-property injection lands, at which point those documents stop being refusals and the entries must go

entries.reason: MEASURED per binding, not guessed. A non-QObject wrapper only leaks if the binding can ALLOCATE it: QtWidgets has 60 such roots but 14 heap-constructible, Controls 98/15, QML 21/7, Quick 98/16. Two are disposable today — QTreeWidgetItem (its destructor detaches from its owner) and QTextStream (nothing in the binding takes one, so its transfer surface is provably empty). The rest still leak, which is the safe error, and ownership-gate-* refuses to let one be enabled without classifying its surface.
entries.remove_when: every disposable non-QObject the binding constructs has an audited transfer surface

entries.reason: MEASURED: destroy a QTreeWidget that owns a QTreeWidgetItem and the item's D wrapper still reports _cpp non-null — checkAlive() never fires. QLayoutItem/QTreeWidgetItem have no destroyed() signal, so nothing invalidates the wrapper. This also rules out the obvious fix: a finalizer that asks parent()/treeWidget() before deleting is CALLING THROUGH the freed pointer, so the query is itself the use-after-free. Ownership has to be dropped at the call that transfers it, not queried at destruction. The probe ASSERTS the gap: when it fails, the gap is closed and this entry must be removed.
entries.remove_when: transfer-in APIs are declared and the emitter drops D ownership at that call, or the types are not D-constructible at all

entries.reason:
THE GUARD EXISTS; THE PATH IS UNTESTED — and the entry said the opposite until 2026-08-13 (critics r13 #6). It claimed that when a C++ constructor throws, nothing owns the __cpp_new block. The emitter produces exactly the scope guard that owns it, and `ctor-guard` walks 1190 constructors to say so on every build. An inventory that keeps a falsified explanation alive is worse than no inventory: it is the failure mode this file was written to prevent, and the linter could not see it because it validates schema and names, not truth.

The residual risk is real and different: no test makes a bound C++ constructor THROW and then checks that the block was freed. The structural gate proves the guard is EMITTED; nothing proves it RUNS. That needs a fixture type whose constructor throws on demand, through the Lippincott layer, with the allocation observed.\n\nDIRECTION (critics r13 #6, second half): this entry has no gap probe because the thing it describes is a MISSING TEST, and a missing test cannot be probed — there is no target that fails today and would pass when the path is exercised, because the target IS the work. Said here rather than left as an empty field: `gap_probes` is for a gap the build can already see, and this one is invisible until someone writes it.
entries.remove_when: a test constructs a bound type whose C++ constructor throws, and observes that the __cpp_new block was freed — the guard proven to RUN, not only to be emitted
entries.title: the ctor scope guard is emitted and gated; the throwing path itself is never run

entries.reason: A pointer a Qt API returns is now BORROWED by default (holder: _ownedByD), which is the safe direction and fixed the ~QThread deadlock. It is not the whole answer: an API that genuinely transfers ownership out (a factory return, QLayout::takeAt) now leaks instead of crashing, and the binding has no per-method ownership metadata to tell the two apart.
entries.remove_when: every pointer-returning method carries ownership metadata (owned / borrowed / transfer-out) instead of a single conservative default

entries.reason: `property alias inner: box.color` — an alias whose target is a VALUE-TYPE property of a child — is refused with "alias target is unsupported". Found while building the two-locals fixture for the CompilationContext question; the alias had to be dropped for the fixture to compile, which is how it surfaced. Aliases onto a child's scalar and onto base properties work. Left as a gap rather than fixed on measurement, not instinct: the shape appears ZERO times across Qt's five Controls styles, and the value-type channel is where a wrongly-typed field once cost eight link failures here.
entries.remove_when: an alias whose target is a child's value-type property compiles, or is refused with a reason

entries.reason:
RESOLVED FOR FIVE OF SIX DOCUMENTS, and the entry is kept for the last one. The cause was two things, not one, and each alone made the matrix worse:

  1. Qt completes parser-status objects in REVERSE creation order (QQmlObjectCreator::finalize drains its stack with pop()). Alone: 233 vs 235.
  2. Qt DEFERS background/contentItem/indicator — Q_CLASSINFO("DeferredPropertyNames") — building them inside its own componentComplete, completing each as it is built, and resizing them only afterwards. Alone: no change at all, because it fixes a difference that only the first one exposes.

Together, and with a third correction to WHEN the deferred children are built — after the ordinary ones have completed, not before, because the engine's finalize drains only what it CREATED and a deferred child was never in that set: Basic 52->54, Fusion 52->54, Universal 50->51, Imagine 41->40, Material unchanged. Total 239 vs 235, -O1 judging 110 vs 108, and optlevels-known.txt EMPTY — the two DelayButtons it carried longest now keep their promise.

What is left is one document: Imagine's TextField, demoted on `data[0].baselineOffset 8.34375` where the engine has 5.34375. Same family and the same arithmetic — the engine measured that Text at height 0 and we measured it at 6 — so a third ordering difference remains inside that document, worth exactly one document and named here rather than hidden in the demoted count.

The order correction alone was worth +3 (236 -> 239) and did NOT fix TextField, which is the evidence that its remaining difference is a THIRD path: the document reads `background` in `topPadding: background ? background.topPadding : 0`, evaluated in the wire phase, and a read forces the deferred build. Under the engine that same read forces it too, so the difference is not the forcing — it is what the control's height is worth at that moment.

TRIED AND REVERTED (2026-08-12): sending the ENGINE-BUILT child down buildProp too, which is where a NinePatchImage background goes because that type is outside our registry. It is the obvious next move and it does not pay — Fusion 54 -> 53 and TextField unchanged, 238 vs 239 over the full matrix. So the remaining difference is not that this background is built eagerly.
entries.remove_when: Imagine's TextField compiles: its data[0] freezes baselineOffset at 5.34375, which means the Text is measured before whatever gives it a height of 6
entries.title: one document still freezes a baseline against the wrong height

entries.reason: An anchor line VALUE now crosses — `anchors.left: parent.left` compiles through copyProp, which moves it between two meta-objects without either side naming QQuickAnchorLine — and AAnchors went from 10 diagnostics to 2. What is left is the DEPENDENCY: `anchors.left: left.right` (anchoring to a sibling) reports "depends on 'left.right', which has no known notify", and an anchor line HAS no notify because a side does not change. Two attempts at the rule failed and both are worth not repeating. (1) 'a member the registry knows with no NOTIFY is constant' is the right rule by Qt's own convention and CANNOT FIRE: the registry does not carry anchor-line properties at all, so the test never matches — inert, reverted. (2) 'wire the OBJECT rather than the member' is right in principle — what can change is which object is on the other end, not the line — and did not move the number either, so the sibling case is reaching this diagnostic through some path other than the copyProp branch. Finding which path is the next step, and it is the third sub-attempt, so it was stopped rather than guessed at. LOCATED, which was the question left open. It is NOT the copyProp branch added for anchors — it is an OLDER copyProp branch above it (the `<obj>.<prop>` -> copyProp/copyGroupProp path), reached first for the sibling form. Swapping the two branches changes nothing, which is how that was established. And there is a second thing wrong at that site, visible once it is the right site: the notify is looked up on `srcType`, which is `g_selfQmlType` — the object BEING CONFIGURED — unless the source is an enclosing object. For `anchors.left: left.right` it therefore asks whether the Rectangle being anchored has a notify for `right`, not whether the SOURCE does. Fixing the lookup is a prerequisite for deciding anything about the missing notify, because today the question is being asked of the wrong object. AND THE LOOKUP FIX ALONE IS INERT, measured: making that branch ask the SOURCE's type instead of the object being configured changes neither AAnchors (2) nor ALayouts (10), because an anchor line has no notify in EITHER type and the refusal comes from wireGroupDeps regardless. Correct and unobservable, so it was reverted rather than landed — it is a prerequisite for the real fix, not the fix, and it needs to arrive WITH the rule that stops treating a missing notify on a constant as fatal.
entries.remove_when: the older `<obj>.<prop>` copyProp branch looks the notify up on the SOURCE's type rather than on the object being configured, and an anchor line — which has no notify because a side does not change — stops being a refusal there; then AAnchors and ALayouts are judged rather than skipped.

entries.reason: AListView compiles with NO diagnostic and is demoted on the frame: its ListModel is built by the engine, its ListElement children are built by the engine, and the list is still empty — `count` 0 against the engine's 3. Not an oversight in the wiring. `ListElement` is not an object anyone appends: QQmlListModel's rows are built by the QML compiler out of the DOCUMENT'S TEXT, so an element instantiated on its own is a shell with nowhere to go. Building a type and then its children separately cannot reproduce that at any level of effort, which sharpens the design note in docs/qmltc-d.md: delegating a CHILD has to hand the engine the subtree's SOURCE, the way --shadow-dir already does for a delegated expression, not a type name and a list of property writes.
entries.remove_when: a child the compiler cannot compile is handed to the engine AS SOURCE — its own text, in the document's context — and AListView's model has three rows

entries.reason: AControlsApp compiles with NO diagnostic and is demoted on the frame. Narrowed: its Label's `text` is right ("level 35%", same as the engine) and its HEIGHT is right (19, which comes from font metrics, so the font and the layout are both there) — only the WIDTH is 0 against 78.65625, and 140 values follow from that one. The Label is completed (componentComplete is emitted for it), so this is not a missing completion. The shape is the one DelayButton's baselineOffset already showed: a Text measures itself ONCE, and if the measurement happens while the text is still empty — `level` reads 0 before the Slider is wired, `text` is set afterwards — the height (a font property) is right and the width (a content property) stays 0. Same family as `completion-order-not-reversed`, and it is the second document to point at it.
entries.remove_when: the Label measures itself after its text arrives — most likely the same fix as completion-order-not-reversed — and AControlsApp is judged rather than demoted

entries.reason: NEITHER SIDE dumps a `var` property, so nothing about one can be measured. Checked: ADynamicProp and AJsLogic both declare one, and no `.qall1` in the whole application corpus carries `items` or `config` — the oracle does not print them either. That is a blind spot in the differential itself, not a compiler gap, and it is the reason work on `var` cannot be judged today. Found by writing the support and then being unable to show it does anything: `property var items: [3,1,4,1,5]` compiles through the engine (the literal's own source handed to QJSEngine::evaluate, stored in the QVariant slot the property already has, counted as DELEGATION so -O1 and -O2 hand the document over) — the call is emitted with the right source and the value is stored, and no gate can see it. Reverted rather than landed, for the same reason two other changes were reverted this session: a change that cannot be shown to do anything must not read as a fix. Reading a var back (`items.length`) is also unsupported, so there is not even an indirect way to observe it. AND THE SKIP IS DELIBERATE, which narrows the fix. The oracle walks every readable property; it drops a QJSValue that does not hold a QObject, with the reason written beside it: "a plain JS object has no comparable text, and one side having `fontInfo` and the other not is a spelling difference, not a defect." That is sound for an OBJECT and not for an ARRAY OF PRIMITIVES — `[3,1,4,1,5]` converts to a QVariantList and has exactly one text, on both sides. So the fix is not "dump var properties", it is "dump a var whose value has comparable text — an array or map of primitives — and keep the documented skip for anything holding a JS object". Both sides have to format it the same way, and our dump excludes QmlVar entirely today, so it is a two-sided harness change before it is a compiler one. WRITTEN AND MEASURED, and it found something on the first run — which is the strongest argument for doing it properly. Making both walkers print a `var` holding an ARRAY OF PRIMITIVES (one separator, no spaces, elements in order, identical on both sides) took FOUR sites, three of them not where expected: the oracle's QJSValue branch, our own C++ walker `qtd_dump_object_as` (the generated writefln list is NOT what `--dumpall` uses — that cost a probe), and a THIRD branch because the engine hands a QJSValue while a `var` we filled ourselves holds the QVariantList that came out of QJSValue::toVariant(); two spellings of one value that must print alike. With that done the minimal case agrees on both sides (`items 3,1,4,1,5`) — and the very first full matrix FAILED, on a line reading `< data[0].sequences` — the engine having a value we print nothing for. THE TARGET IS NOT IDENTIFIED, and two guesses were checked and both fell: `CDeepRead`, read off a log line where two builds' output interleaved, has a plain QQuickRectangle at data[0] with no such property (QQmlListReference, checked); `QEnumOnlyType`, the only document in any corpus with a `Shortcut`, prints `data[0].sequence` — SINGULAR, value 9 — and no `sequences`. So the finding is real (a whole property kind was hiding a difference) and the document is not known. Whoever redoes it should capture the failure with a SERIAL build, or read the per-target `.qall`/`.dall` beside the check rather than the interleaved log, which is what defeated two attempts here.
entries.remove_when: the `data[0].sequences` difference is reproduced with its target identified — from the per-target dumps, not the interleaved log — and then the four-site change lands together with `property var x: <JS literal>`, which is written and works

entries.title: a property the document declares on a child we did not generate a class for lands on the wiring object
entries.reason:
Qt's Material ToolButton writes `readonly property bool square: control.contentItem.width <= control.contentItem.height` on a Ripple — a type outside our registry, so the child is ENGINE-BUILT: a wrapper holding the real object in `__inst`. The declared property becomes a @Property FIELD ON THE WRAPPER, where nothing that reads the tree can see it. The engine puts it on the object. Measured: `background.square true` is present in the engine's dump and absent in ours, with NO DIAGNOSTIC — a silently dropped declared member, which is the worse half.

TRIED AND REVERTED (2026-08-12): mirroring the value onto the instance with setPropAny, guarded by `is(typeof(__inst))` so it costs nothing in an ordinary class. It runs, and it does not show: setPropAny creates a DYNAMIC property (QObject::setProperty on an undeclared name), which lives in dynamicPropertyNames() and not in the meta-object, and every walk of the tree — ours and the census's — reads the meta-object. So the value is there and unreachable.

What it needs is the property IN the meta-object, which is what the engine does for a QML-declared property: QQmlOpenMetaObject, or the QMetaObjectBuilder path this project already uses for D-defined @QObject types, applied to an object someone else built. Worth exactly one document today (Material's ToolButton) and worth more than that as a class: a declared member that disappears without a word is the failure mode the certainty levels exist to catch.
entries.remove_when: Material's ToolButton dumps `background.square true`, which means a document-declared property on an engine-built child is on the OBJECT and reachable through its meta-object

entries.title: the only Material frame left, and the census agrees on every value it reads
entries.reason:
Material's SliderHandle renders as a filled pink circle under the engine and as nothing under ours, and BOTH sides dump `data[0].color #00000000` — transparent. So the pixel that differs is not any value the census reads, which is the opposite of every other document in this file.

The document explains why it is delicate: `readonly property var control: parent`, and both colours are `root.control ? <Material colour> : "transparent"`. Standalone the item has no parent, so `control` is null and both colours ARE transparent — which is what both sides dump. The engine's frame is pink anyway, so under the o3 gate's render its item has a parent that ours does not, and the value dumped is not the value drawn.

That makes this a question about the RENDER CONTEXT the two harnesses give the object, not about the compiler: both `color` bindings are already DELEGATED to the engine here, so the expression is the engine's own. Named rather than left inside a demoted count, because a difference the value axis cannot see is exactly the kind this project keeps being surprised by.
entries.remove_when: Material's SliderHandle renders identically, which means the object is drawn in the same parent context on both sides — or the difference is shown to be a real value one after all

entries.title: the Imagine style's impl types are absent, so every one of its documents delegates
entries.reason:
`NinePatchImageSelector` and the rest of QtQuick.Controls.Imagine.impl are not in the binding, so every Imagine document builds those objects through the ENGINE and delegates their `states: [ {...} ]` binding. Measured 2026-08-12: after the dynamic leaf read landed, Imagine's documents report `0 skipped, 0 weakly typed` and exactly one delegation each — that one. It is why `-O1` compiles NOTHING in that style and why the level judge excludes it as vacuous.\n\nThis is a GENERATION question, not a compiler one: compiling `states` would buy nothing while the objects themselves are engine-built, because -O1 refuses on that axis first. Recorded here with a gap probe so the day it stops being true is a red line rather than a discovery.

O gap probe carrega a ASSINATURA da falha (critics r14 #7): exit e um pedaço do diagnóstico. Sem ela, ferramenta ausente, import partido, crash ou mudança de CLI liam-se todos como "o buraco continua aberto" — um expected-fail sem assinatura, que é o que este ficheiro existe para deixar de ser.
entries.remove_when: `qmltc-pedantic-imagine-label` passes — Imagine's Label compiles with ZERO delegations, which means the style's impl types are typeable

entries.title: the full matrix fails intermittently under concurrency; the affected target moves
entries.reason:
Observed on 2026-08-14 in FOUR documents across three gates, each with a different signature: `qmltcc-CBareObj-all-ldc2` and `CDefaultProp` disagreeing on dumped values, `qmltc-optlevels-ATile` reporting `-O1 does not link`, `qmltc-optlevels-ASignalCross` reporting `-O1 and -O2 disagree`, and `qmltc-optlevels-AStates` reporting `-O1 disagrees with the engine`. Every one passes in isolation (measured 6/6, 3/3 and 3/3 on the first three) and a full `./build --single` run finished green (rc=0, ~65 min against ~20 parallel).

THE LIST OF TARGETS BELOW IS ILLUSTRATIVE, NOT EXHAUSTIVE. The first version of this entry named three; the next parallel run produced a fourth. What identifies this risk is the CONDITION — a failure that appears only in the full parallel matrix, never in isolation, and never with `--single` — not the particular document that happened to lose the race.

What that eliminates: a deterministic defect in the compiler, the oracle or the comparator, which would fail identically on one thread. What it does not establish: the cause. The probable mechanism is already documented in this repository, in the comment on `qmltcTool`: `guarded` stops two WRITERS from colliding but does not stop a target from executing or reading `qmltc-d`, `libbinding_*.a`, `qtd_render.o` or `qtd_qmltc_app.o` while another relinks them. Each gate then reports the symptom in its own vocabulary, which is why one incident looks like four.

MEASURED SERIALLY, TWICE. `./build --single` finished green (rc=0, ~65 min against ~20 parallel) but did not reach the nested `./build` calls inside expected-fails-run, so that phase stayed parallel. Repeated as `QTD_BUILD_FLAGS=--single ./build --single`, which does cover them: green again, ~75 min. So there is no deterministic instance anywhere in the matrix — not in the ~1150 top-level targets and not in the 26 nested probes.

Cost, for whoever repeats this: serialising the top level is ~3x and is cheap enough for routine diagnosis; serialising the nested probes as well is ~4x and is a one-off experiment, not a practice — the 26 probes each pay their own build startup with nothing shared.

One green serial run has modest power on its own; two, at both levels, is what this entry rests on.

HOW OFTEN: five red runs in roughly nineteen full parallel runs of this session — about 1 in 4 — against 0 in 2 serial ones. That rate matters for whoever attacks the cause: an instrumented run has a good chance of catching the incident live, where 1 in 50 would mean automating dozens of runs first. The fifth occurrence was `AStates` reporting `-O1 does not link`, the SAME signature as `ATile` and AFTER the dependency fix below — so that fix did not cover every artifact the link consumes. An earlier version of this entry said the archives and `qmltc-d` were still undeclared. THAT WAS WRONG — read the target: `[tool, Target(script), Target(e), bind.gen, qtdBindLib(bind, "ldc2"), bind.shims]`. They are all dependencies already.

And that is the point. DECLARING A DEPENDENCY DOES NOT PROTECT A READER. In this backend a dependency means "build it before me if it is stale", not "do not rewrite it while I run": another target that depends on the same archive can trigger its rebuild DURING this link, and `guarded` only stops two writers from colliding — the reader holds no lock at all. So the dependency fix below was a real defect fixed (proven by deletion) and could never have cured this: the intermittency was never about missing edges, it is about the absence of reader/writer exclusion on shared artifacts.

One real defect was found and fixed while chasing this — `qmltc-optlevels-*` linked against `qtd_render.o`/`qtd_qmltc_app.o` without declaring them, testing with `[ -f ]` and linking whatever was on disk. Fixed and proven by deletion, and it did NOT stop the intermittency: ASignalCross and AStates failed afterwards with different signatures.
entries.remove_when: the shared-artifact reader/writer race is either proven and fixed, or ruled out by instrumenting the backend to record when a node is re-scheduled

entries.title: the Qt5 parity artifacts are built with 5.15.19 and the licence matrix records 5.15.17
entries.reason:
Round 18 #2: the product gate verified whichever Qt release it queried first (Qt6) and then applied a module-only allowlist to every line of the link manifest — including two archives built with Qt 5.15.19, a release nobody had read. The matrix is now keyed by (release, module) and every artifact is judged against the release that produced it, so those two archives and the four Qt5 specs are refused by name.

That refusal is CORRECT and is why this entry exists rather than a new matrix row. The rows for Qt5 say 5.15.17 because that is the release whose licensing was actually read; writing 5.15.19 on them would have been inventing the record, and it was nearly done automatically by a rewrite script before being caught.

Two honest resolutions, both requiring a decision this build cannot make: read Qt's licensing for 5.15.19 and record it, or stop building Qt5 parity artifacts. Note that the Qt5 archives are NOT installed — the package is built from the Qt6 qtwidgets binding — so the exposure is a test artifact, not a shipped one; that is a reason to fix it calmly, not a reason to call it verified.
entries.remove_when: 5.15.19 is read and recorded in docs/qt-license-matrix.tsv, or the Qt5 parity build is retired
